_source.chapter: Making a Special Effort for Ones Guest
_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): لا يَتَكَلَّفَنَّ أحَدٌ لِضَيفِهِ ما لا يَقدِرُ .
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘No one should go to troubles that they cannot afford for a guest.

_source.chapter: Making a Special Effort for Ones Guest
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): إذا أتاكَ أخُوك فَآتِهِ بما عِندَك، وإذا دَعَوتَهُ فَتَكَلَّفْ لَهُ .
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, ‘If your brother comes to your house [uninvited] then offer him whatever you have in the house, and if you invite him, then make a special effort for him.

_source.chapter: Making a Special Effort for Ones Guest
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الرِّضا (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): دَعا رجُلٌ أميرَ المؤمنينَ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) فقالَ لَهُ: قد أجَبتُكَ على أن تَضمَنَ لي ثلاثَ خِصالٍ . قال: وما هِيَ يا أميرَ المؤمنينَ ؟ قال: لا تُدخِلْ عَلَيَّ شيئاً مِن خارِجٍ، ولا تَدَّخِرْ عَنّي شيئاً في البيتِ، ولا تُجحِفْ بالعِيالِ . قالَ: ذاكَ لكَ يا أميرَ المؤمنينَ، فأجابَهُ عليُّ بنُ أبي طالبٍ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ).
_source.english: Imam al-Rida (AS) narrated, ‘A man once invited the Commander of the Faithful, Ali (AS) for a meal, so Imam said to him, ‘I will accept your invitation provided you fulfil three conditions. The man asked, ‘And what are they, O Commander of the Faithful? to which he replied, ‘Do not bring any special food from outside for me, do not preserve anything in the house especially for me, and do not impose any difficulty on your family. The man replied, ‘You shall have that O Commander of the Faithful and Ali b. Abi Talib accepted his invitation.
_source.cited_from: Uyoun Akhbar al-Ridha (AS), volume:2, p. 42, number:138

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): مَن أحَبَّ أن يُحِبَّهُ اللّهُ ورسولُهُ فَليَأكُلْ مَعَ ضَيفِهِ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘Whoever wants to be loved by Allah and His Prophet should eat with his guest.

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): إذا دُعِيَ أحَدُكُم إلى طَعامٍ فلا يَستَتبِعَنَّ وَلَدَهُ؛ فإنّهُ إن فَعَلَ ذلكَ كانَ حَراماً ودَخَلَ عاصياً.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘When one of you is invited for a meal, he must not bring along his son with him too, for verily it is prohibited for him to do so and he enters the house unlawfully.

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): الضَّيفُ يُلطَفُ لَيلَتَينِ، فإذا كانتِ اللَّيلةُ الثالثةُ فهُو مِن أهلِ البيتِ يَأكُلُ ما أدرَكَ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘A guest may expect to be honoured for two nights, then from the third night onwards he is considered to be one of the family and must eat whatever he gets.

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): الضِّيافَةُ أوَّلُ يَومٍ والثاني والثالثُ، وما بعدَ ذلكَ فإنّها صَدَقةٌ تَصَدّق بها علَيهِ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘Hospitality towards a guest is incumbent for the first day, the second day and the third day. After that, anything you give him is considered as charity towards him on your behalf.

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): الوَليمَةُ أوَّلُ يومٍ حَقٌّ، والثاني مَعروفٌ، وما زادَ رياءٌ وسُمعَةٌ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘Hosting a banquet the first day is reasonable, the second day is an act of courtesy, and any more than that is showing-off and seeking repute.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الباقرُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): إذا دَخَلَ أحَدُكُم على أخيهِ في رَحلِهِ فَلْيَقعُدْ حيثُ يَأمُرُ صاحِبُ الرَّحلِ؛ فإنّ صاحِبَ الرَّحلِ أعرَفُ بِعَورَةِ بَيتِهِ مِن الداخِلِ علَيهِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Baqir (AS) said, ‘When someone enters the house of his fellow brother, he must sit wherever the host tells him to sit for the owner of the house knows the flaws of his own house better than the guest.

_source.arabic: ابنِ أبي يَعفورٍ: رأيتُ عِند أبي عبدِ اللّهِ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ضَيفاً، فقامَ يَوماً في بعضِ الحَوائج، فنَهاهُ عن ذلكَ، وقامَ بنفسِهِ إلى تلك الحاجَةِ، وقالَ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): نَهى رسولُ اللّهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ) عَن أن يُستَخدَمَ الضَّيفُ.
_source.english: Ibn Abi Yaafur narrated, ‘I saw a guest once at Abi Aabdillahs [i.e. Imam al-Sadiq (AS)] house, who stood up to get something he needed, so Imam refused for him to do so, and stood up to get it himself, saying, ‘The Prophet of Allah (AS) prohibited that a guest be allowed to do work.

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): مِن سَعادَةِ المَرءِ المُسلمِ المَسكَنُ الواسِعُ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, 'Part of a Muslim's prosperity is living in spacious housing.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الباقرُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): مِن شَقاءِ العَيشِ ضِيقُ المَنزِلِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Baqir (AS) said, 'A misfortunate way of life entails living in a cramped house.

_source.chapter: Caution Against Building More Housing Than Necessary for One's Living
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): مِنَ العَناءِ أنَّ المَرءَ يَجمَعُ ما لا يَأكُلُ ويَبنِي ما لا يَسكُنُ ، ثُمّ يَخرُجُ إلى اللّهِ تعالى لا مالاً حَمَلَ ، ولا بِناءً نَقَلَ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, 'It is a distressful situation that man amasses what he does not eat and builds wherein he does not live, then he goes to Allah, most High, neither carrying the wealth with him, nor shifting the building!

_source.chapter: Caution Against Building More Housing Than Necessary for One's Living
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): كُلُّ بِناءٍ ليسَ بِكَفافٍ فهُو وبالٌ على صاحِبِهِ يَومَ القِيامَةِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, 'Every building exceeding the bounds of sufficiency will be a dire curse on its owner on the Day of Resurrection.

_source.chapter: Caution Against Building More Housing Than Necessary for One's Living
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): مَن بَنى فَوقَ مَسكَنِهِ كُلِّفَ حَملَهُ يَومَ القِيامَةِ .
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, 'He who builds in addition to his own house [unnecessarily] will be made to bear its burden on the Day of Resurrection.

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): مَن باعَ داراً ثُمّ لم يَجعَلْ ثَمَنَها في مِثلِها لَم يُبارَكْ لَهُ فيها .
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, 'Whoever sells a house and does not invest the money in something of similar value will not be blessed in it [his money].

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): مَن باعَ مِنكم داراً أو عَقاراً ، فَلْيَعلَمْ أنَّهُ مالٌ قَمَنٌ أن لا يُبارَكَ لَهُ فيهِ إلّا أن يَجعَلَهُ في مِثلِهِ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, 'Whoever from among you sells a house or some real estate, then let him bear in mind that the money acquired is not worthy of being blessed unless he invests it in something of similar value.

_source.arabic: إرشاد القلوب : في حديثِ المِعراجِ : ما عَرَفَني عَبدٌ وخَشَعَ لي إلّا خَشَعَ لَهُ كُلُّ شيءٍ.
_source.english: In the tradition recounting the Prophets Ascension, Allah says, ‘No sooner does a servant come to know Me and humble himself before Me than everything is humbled before him.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : نِعْمَ عَونُ الدُّعاءِ الخُشوعُ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The best aid for supplication is humility.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ زينُ العابدينَ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ في الدُّعاءِ ـ : وأَعوذُ بكَ مِن نَفْسٍ لا تَقْنَعُ وبَطْنٍ لا يَشْبَعُ ، وقَلبٍ لا يَخْشَعُ .
_source.english: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) said in his supplication, ‘I seek refuge in you from a soul which is never content, a stomach which is not satisfied and a heart which has no humility.

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ) : أمّا عَلامَةُ الخاشِعِ فأربَعةٌ : مُراقَبَةُ اللّهِ في السِّرِّ والعَلانِيَةِ ، ورُكوبُ الجَميلِ ، والتَّفَكُّرُ ليَومِ القِيامَةِ ، والمُناجاةُ للّهِ .
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘There are four distinguishing marks of the humble ones: they pay constant attention to Allah in private and in public, they carry out good works, they contemplate about the Day of Resurrection, and they engage in intimate supplication with Allah.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : مَن خَشَعَ قَلبُهُ خَشَعَتْ جَوارِحُهُ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘One whose heart is humble, his limbs also humble themselves.

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): أشَدُّ الناسِ حِساباً يَومَ القِيامَةِ المَكفِيُّ الفارِغُ، إن كانَ الشُغلُ مَجهَدَةً فالفَراغُ مَفسَدَةٌ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘The one to be the most harshly judged on the Day of Resurrection will be the capable yet idle [people]. If work is endeavor, idleness is corruptive.

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): إنَّ اللّهَ يُبغِضُ الصَّحيحَ الفارِغَ، لا في شُغلِ الدنيا ولا في شُغلِ الآخِرَةِ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘Verily Allah hates the healthy-bodied idle person, who is neither concerned with his worldly life, nor the Hereafter.
_source.cited_from: Sharhe Nahj al-Balagha li B. Abi al-Hadid, volume:17, p. 146

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): خَلَّتانِ كثيرٌ مِن الناسِ فيهِما مَفتونٌ: الصِّحَّةُ والفَراغُ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘There are two things most people are tested with: health and idleness.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): مِن الفَراغِ تكونُ الصَّبوَةُ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘From idleness comes desire.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): اِعلَمْ أنَّ الدنيا دارُ بَلِيَّةٍ لم يَفرُغْ صاحِبُها فيها قَطُّ ساعَةً إلّا كانَت فَرغَتُهُ علَيهِ حَسرَةً يَومَ القِيامَةِ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Know that the world is a place of trial wherein there is no time a person can afford to be idle, for that time will be a source of regret for him on the Day of Resurrection.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): ما أحَقَّ الإنسانَ أن تكونَ لَهُ ساعَةٌ لا يَشغَلُهُ عَنها شاغِلٌ!
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘How deserving man is of having an hour where no one disturbs him!

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): إنْ يَكُنِ الشُّغلُ مَجهَدَةً فاتِّصالُ الفَراغِ مَفسَدَةٌ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘If work is endeavor, then continuous idleness is corruptive.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ زينُ العابدينَ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ في دعائهِ ـ: وَاشغَلْ قُلوبَنا بِذِكرِكَ عن كُلِّ ذِكرٍ، وألسِنَتَنا بشُكرِكَ عن كُلِّ شُكرٍ، وجَوارِحَنا بطاعَتِكَ عن كُلِّ طاعَةٍ، فإن قَدَّرتَ لنا فَراغاً مِن شُغلٍ فاجعَلْهُ فَراغَ سلامَةٍ، لاتُدرِكُنا فيهِ تَبِعَةٌ، ولاتَلحَقُنا فيهِ سَأمَةٌ، حتّى يَنصَرِفَ عنّا كُتّابُ السَّيّئاتِ بصَحيفَةٍ خالِيَةٍ مِن ذِكرِ سَيِّئاتِنا، ويَتَوَلّى كُتّابُ الحَسَناتِ عنّا مَسرورِينَ.
_source.english: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) said in his supplication, '…and divert our hearts from every other act of remembrance through Your remembrance, our tongues from every other act of thanksgiving through [being preoccupied with] thanking You, our limbs from every other act of obedience through [being preoccupied with] obedience to You! If You have ordained for us idleness in an occupation, make it an idleness of safety, wherein no ill consequence visits us nor weariness overtakes us as a result! Then the writers of evil deeds may depart from us with a page empty of the mention of our evil deeds, and the writers of good deeds may leave us happy with the good deeds of ours which they have written.'

_source.arabic: الإمامُ زينُ العابدينَ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ مِن دعائهِ في مكارمِ الأخلاقِ ـ: اللّهُمَّ صَلِّ على محمّدٍ وآلِهِ، واكفِني ما يَشغَلُنِي الاهتِمامُ بهِ، واستَعمِلْني بما تَسألُنِي غَدا عَنهُ، واستَفرِغْ أيّامِي فيما خَلَقتَنِي لَهُ.
_source.english: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) said in his supplication, 'O Allah, bless Muhammad and his Household, and spare me the concerns which distract me, employ me in that which You will ask me about tomorrow, and let me pass my days [engaged] in that for which You have created me!'

_source.arabic: الإمامُ زينُ العابدينَ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ أيضا ـ: وارزُقْنِي صِحَّةً في عِبادَةٍ، وفَراغاً في زَهادَةٍ.
_source.english: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS), in his supplication said, '…and grant me health for the sake of worshipping [You], and idleness for the sake of reclusion.'

_source.arabic: الإمامُ زينُ العابدينَ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ مِن دعائهِ في يومِ عَرَفَةَ ـ: وأذِقْني طَعمَ الفَراغِ لِما تُحِبُّ بِسَعَةٍ مِن سَعَتِكَ، والاجتِهادِ فيما يُزلِفُ لَدَيكَ وعِندَك، وأتحِفْني بتُحفَةٍ من تُحَفاتِكَ، واجعَلْ تِجارَتِي رابِحَةً، وكَرَّتي غيرَ خاسِرَةٍ، وأخِفنِي مَقامَكَ، وشَوِّقْني لِقاءَكَ.
_source.english: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) said in his supplication on the day of Aarafa, 'Let me taste, through some of Your boundless plenty, the flavour of being free for what You love, and striving in what brings about proximity with You and to You, and give me a gift from among Your gifts! Make my commerce profitable and my return without loss, fill me with fear of Your station, and make me yearn for the meeting with You.'

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الكاظمُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): إنّ اللّهَ تعالى لَيُبغِضُ العَبدَ النَّوَّامَ، إنّ اللّهَ تعالى لَيُبغِضُ العَبدَ الفارِغَ .
_source.english: Imam al-Kazim (AS) said, 'Verily Allah, most High, hates the servant who sleeps much; verily Allah, most High, hates the idle servant.'

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : الجَهلُ أدْوَأُ الدّاءِ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Ignorance is the worst affliction.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : الجَهلُ مُمِيتُ الأحْياءِ ومُخَلِّدُ الشَّقاءِ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Ignorance is death for the living and perpetuates wretchedness.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : الجَهلُ فَسادُ كُلِّ أمْرٍ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Ignorance is the ruination of every affair.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : الجَهلُ أصْلُ كُلِّ شَرٍّ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Ignorance is the root of every evil.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : الحِرْصُ والشَّرَهُ والبُخْلُ نَتيجَةُ الجَهلِ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Greed, voracity, and stinginess are a result of ignorance.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ العسكريُّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : الجَهلُ خَصْمٌ .
_source.english: Imam al-Askari (AS) said, ‘Ignorance is an enemy.

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ) : إنَّ الجاهِلَ مَن عَصى اللّهَ وإنْ كانَ جَميلَ المَنظَرِ عَظيمَ الخَطَرِ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘The ignorant is one who disobeys Allah, even if he is beautiful to look at and of great importance.

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ) : صِفةُ الجاهِلِ : أنْ يَظلِمَ مَن خالَطَهُ ، ويَتَعدّى على مَن هُو دُونَهُ ، ويَتطاوَلَ على مَن هُو فَوقَهُ ، كلامُهُ بغَيرِ تَدَبُّرٍ....
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘The characteristic of an ignorant person is that he oppresses whoever he associates with, acts unjustly towards his subordinates, flatters his superiors, and his speech is without deliberation.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : الجاهِلُ لا يَعْرِفُ تَقْصيرَهُ ولا يَقبلُ مِن النَّصيحِ لَهُ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘An ignorant person does not see his own shortcomings and is not willing to accept any advice concerning them.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : الجاهِلُ مَيِّتٌ وإنْ كانَ حَيّاً.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘An ignorant person is dead, even though he is living.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : الجاهِلُ مَنِ انْخَدَعَ لِهَواهُ وغُرورِهِ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The ignorant is one who has allowed himself to be deceived by his desires and whims.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : لا تَرى الجاهِلَ إلّا مُفْرِطاً أو مُفَرِّطاً .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘You will not see an ignorant person except that he is either committing excess in what he does or falling short of what he ought to do.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : إنَّما الجاهِلُ مَنِ اسْتَعْبَدتْهُ المَطالِبُ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The ignorant is one whose desires have enslaved him.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : الجاهِلُ عَبدُ شَهْوتِه .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The ignorant is a slave of his desires.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : عَملُ الجاهِلِ وبَالٌ ، وعِلمُهُ ضلالٌ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The deeds of the ignorant are doomed and his knowledge is error.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : إنَّ الجاهِلَ مَن عَدّ نَفسَهُ ـ بما جَهِلَ مِن مَعرفَةِ العِلمِ ـ عالِماً ، وبِرَأيهِ مُكْتَفياً ، فمَا يَزالُ للعُلماءِ مُباعِداً وعَلَيهِم زارِياً ، ولِمَن خَالفَهُ مُخَطِّئاً ، ولِمَا لَم يَعْرِفْ مِن الاُمورِ مُضَلِّلاً ، فإذا وَردَ علَيهِ مِن الاُمورِ ما لَم يَعْرِفْهُ أنْكَرَهُ وكَذّبَ بهِ وقالَ بجَهالَتِهِ : ما أعْرِفُ هذا! وما أراهُ كانَ! وما أظُنُّ أنْ يَكونَ! وأنّى كانَ؟! وذلكَ لِثِقَتِهِ بِرَأْيِه وقِلَّةِ مَعْرِفَتِهِ بجَهالَتِهِ! فمَا يَنْفَكُّ بما يَرى مِمّا يَلْتَبِسُ علَيهِ رأيُهُ مِمّا لا يَعْرِفُ للجَهلِ مُسْتَفيداً، وللحقِّ مُنكِراً، وفي الجَهالَةِ مُتَحيِّراً، وعن طَلَبِ العِلمِ مُسْتَكبِراً.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The ignorant is one who considers himself knowledgeable about what he is [in actual fact] ignorant of, and he is content with his own opinion. His attachment to scholars only increases his estrangement [from knowledge] since he is constantly finding fault with them. He deems invalid the views of those who oppose him, and that which he does not understand he sees as fallacious. If he comes across something that he does not know, he denies it and falsifies it saying, ‘I have never heard of this! or ‘I do not see it as possible! or ‘How can it be! or ‘Where is this from? This is due to his confidence in his own opinion and the paucity of his awareness of his own ignorance.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): مِن أخلاقِ الجاهِلِ الإجابَةُ قَبلَ أنْ يَسمَعَ، والمُعارَضَةُ قَبلَ أنْ يَفْهَمَ، والحُكْمُ بما لا يَعْلَمُ.
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, ‘The attributes of the ignorant are that: he answers before listening, objects before understanding, and passes judgment on that which he does not know.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الهاديُّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : الجاهِلُ أسِيرُ لِسانِهِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Hadi (AS) said, ‘The ignorant is a prisoner of his tongue.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : أجْهلُ النّاسِ المُغَترُّ بقَولِ مادِحٍ مُتَملِّقٍ ، يُحسِّنُ لَهُ القَبيحَ ويُبغِّضُ إلَيهِ النَّصيحَ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The most ignorant of people is one who is deluded by the praise of a flatterer who beautifies evil to him and renders a sincere advice detestable.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : غايةُ الجَهلِ تَبَجُّحُ المَرءِ بِجَهْلِهِ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The utter extremity of ignorance is for one to glorify his own ignorance.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : أعظَمُ الجَهلِ جَهلُ الإنسانِ أمرَ نَفْسِهِ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The greatest form of ignorance is for a person to be ignorant of the condition of his own self.

_source.chapter: What is Sufficient to be Considered Ignorant
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : كَفى بالمرءِ جَهلاً أنْ يَرتَكِبَ ما نَهى عَنهُ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘It suffices for one to be considered ignorant if he commits that which is forbidden.

_source.chapter: What is Sufficient to be Considered Ignorant
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : حَسْبكَ مِن الجَهلِ أنْ تُعجَبَ بعِلْمِكَ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Self-admiration in ones knowledge is sufficient to be considered ignorance.

_source.chapter: What is Sufficient to be Considered Ignorant
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : كفى بالمرءِ جَهلاً أنْ يَجْهَلَ قَدْرَهُ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘It suffices as ignorance to be unaware of ones status.

_source.chapter: What is Sufficient to be Considered Ignorant
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : لا تَتَكلّمْ بكُلِّ ما تَعلَمُ فكَفى بذلكَ جَهلاً .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Do not utter all that you know since that is enough to be considered ignorance.

_source.chapter: What is Sufficient to be Considered Ignorant
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : كفى بخَشيَةِ اللّهِ عِلْما ، وكفى بالاغْتِرارِ باللّهِ جَهْلاً .
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, ‘[Possessing] fear of Allah suffices as knowledge, and being conceited towards Him suffices as ignorance.

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ) : مِن الجَهل أنْ تُظهِرَ كلَّ ماعَلِمْتَ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘Ignorance is to display all that you know.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : الرُّكونُ إلى الدُّنيا مَع ما تُعايِنُ مِنها جَهلٌ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Relying on this world in spite of all that you face therein is ignorance.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : رَغْبتُكَ في المُستَحيلِ جَهلٌ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Your desire for the impossible is ignorance.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الحسنُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ لمّا سألَهُ أبوه عن تفسيرِ الجَهلِ ـ : سُرعةُ الوُثوبِ علَى الفُرْصةِ قبلَ الاسْتِمْكانِ مِنها ، والامْتِناعُ عنِ الجَوابِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Hasan (AS), when his father asked him the meaning of ignorance, said, ‘It is hastening to snatch up an opportunity before having made oneself capable [of fulfilling it], and it is to refuse to answer.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : الجَهلُ في ثلاثٍ : في تَبدُّلِ الإخْوانِ ، والمُنابَذَةِ بغَيرِ بَيانٍ ، والتَّجَسُّسِ عمّا لا يَعني.
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, ‘Ignorance lies in three things: in compromising ones brothers, declaring war without the command to do so, and spying into affairs that do not concern one.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ العسكريُّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : مِن الجَهلِ الضّحكُ من غيرِ عَجَبٍ .
_source.english: Imam al-Askari (AS) said, ‘Ignorance is to laugh without any reason.

_source.chapter: Man is Averse To What He is Ignorant of
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : النّاسُ أعْداءُ ما جَهِلوهُ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘People are antagonists of what they are ignorant of.

_source.chapter: Man is Averse To What He is Ignorant of
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : مَن جَهِلَ شيئا عابَهُ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘He who is ignorant of something finds fault with it.

_source.chapter: Man is Averse To What He is Ignorant of
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : قلتُ أرْبَعاً أنزلَ اللّهُ تعالى تَصديقي بها في كِتابِهِ...قُلتُ : مَن جَهِلَ شيئا عادَاهُ ، فأنْزلَ اللّهُ: «بَلْ كَذَّبوا بِما لَم يُحيطوا بِعلْمِهِ».
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘I have said four things which Allah has verified with verses He has revealed in His Book … I said: ‘He who is ignorant of something will oppose it, and He revealed: “Rather, they deny that whose knowledge they do not comprehend”.

_source.chapter: Man is Averse To What He is Ignorant of
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : لا تُعادوا ما تَجهَلونَ ؛ فإنَّ أكثرَ العِلمِ فيما لا تَعْرِفونَ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Do not oppose that which you are ignorant of; for most knowledge lies in that which you cannot fathom.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : يَجِبُ على الإمامِ أنْ يَحْبِسَ الفُسّاقَ مِن العُلَماءِ ، والجُهّالَ مِن الأطِبّاءِ ، والمَفالِيسَ مِن الأكْرِياءِ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘It is incumbent upon the Imam to imprison the reckless from among the scholars, the ignorant from among the physicians, and the bankrupt from among the lease-holders.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : إذا ارْتَدَّتِ المَرأةُ عنِ الإسلامِ لَم تُقْتَلْ ، ولكنْ تُحْبَسُ أبداً.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘If a Muslim woman becomes an apostate, abandoning Islam, she is not killed but is imprisoned for life.

_source.arabic: الكافي : إنّ أميرَ المؤمنينَ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) كانَ لا يَرى الحَبْسَ إلّا في ثلاثٍ : رجُلٌ أكلَ مالَ اليَتيمِ، أو غَصَبهُ ، أو رجُلٌ اؤتُمِنَ على أمانَةٍ فَذَهبَ بِها.
_source.english: It is narrated in al-Kafi: Verily the Commander of the Faithful (AS) restricted imprisonment to only three cases: a man consuming the property of an orphan unlawfully, or usurping it, or a man who takes off with what he has been entrusted with.

_source.chapter: Jailing the Warrantor until the Return of the Warranted
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : اُتيَ أميرُ المؤمنينَ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) برجُلٍ قد تَكفَّلَ بنَفْسِ رجُلٍ، فحَبسَهُ وقالَ: اطلُبْ صاحِبَكَ.
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, ‘A man was brought to the Commander of the Faithful (AS), who had bailed the life of another man. He imprisoned him, saying, ‘Ask for your companion now.
_source.chapter_ar: حَبسُ الكَفيلِ إلى حينِ حُضورِ المَكفولِ

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الباقرُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ في رجُلٍ أمَرَ رجُلاً بقَتلِ رجُلٍ فقَتلَهُ ـ : يُقْتَلُ بهِ الّذي قَتَلَهُ ، ويُحْبَسُ الآمِرُ بقَتْلِهِ في السِّجْنِ حتّى يَموتَ.
_source.english: Imam al-Baqir (AS) said, about a man who had ordered another man to kill someone, which he had done ‘He who killed him must be killed, and he who ordered the killing must be imprisoned until he dies.

_source.chapter: Imprisonment after Punishment and Acknowledgment of the Truth
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : حَبْسُ الإمامِ بعدَ الحَدِّ ظُلْمٌ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘It is unjust for the Imam to imprison the culprit after punishment.
_source.chapter_ar: الحَبسُ بَعدَ إقامَةِ الحَدِّ ومَعرِفَةِ الحَقِّ

_source.chapter: Imprisonment after Punishment and Acknowledgment of the Truth
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : الحَبسُ بَعدَ معرِفَةِ الحقِّ ظُلْمٌ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Imprisonment after acknowledgment of the truth is injustice.
_source.chapter_ar: الحَبسُ بَعدَ إقامَةِ الحَدِّ ومَعرِفَةِ الحَقِّ

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : أنَّهُ [عَلِيّا] كانَ يَعْرِضُ السّجونَ في كُلِّ يَومِ جُمُعةٍ؛ فمَن كانَ علَيهِ حَدٌّ أقامَهُ، ومَن لَم يَكُن علَيهِ حَدٌّ خلّى سَبيلَهُ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) used to inspect the prisons every Friday; he punished the convicts and released those who had no charge against them.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) : على الإمامِ أنْ يُخرِجَ المَحْبوسينَ في الدَّينِ يَومَ الجُمُعةِ إلى الجُمُعةِ ، ويَومَ العِيدِ إلى العِيدِ ، فيُرسِلَ مَعهُم ، فإذا قَضَوُا الصَّلاةَ والعِيدَ رَدّهُم إلى السِّجنِ .
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, ‘It is the duty of the Imam to release the prisoners on financial charges on Fridays and Ayd [religious festivals] to observe the congregational prayer. He may send them guarded, and when they complete the prayers and the feast, he should return them to the prison.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ عليه السلام : من اُلهِمَ العِصمَةَ أمِنَ الزَّلَلَ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘He who is divinely granted infallibility is safe from error.

_source.arabic: معاني الأخبار عن الإمامِ الكاظم عن آبائه عن الإمامِ زينِ العابدينَ: الإمامُ مِنّا لا يَكونُ إلّا مَعصوماً، ولَيسَتِ العِصمَةُ في ظاهِرِ الخِلقَةِ فيُعرَفَ بِها ، ولِذلكَ لا يَكونُ إلّا مَنصوصاً. فقيلَ لَهُ: يَابنَ رَسولِ اللّهِ ، فَما مَعنَى المَعصومِ؟ فقالَ: هُوَ المُعتَصِمُ بِحَبلِ اللّهِ ، وحَبلُ اللّهِ هُوَ القُرآنُ، لا يَفتَرِقانِ إلى يَومِ القِيامَةِ، والإمامُ يَهدي إلَى القُرآنِ، والقُرآنُ يَهدي إلَى الإمامِ ، وذلكَ قَولُ اللّهِ عزَّوجلَّ: «إنَّ هذا القُرآنَ يَهْدي لِلَّتي هِيَ أقْوَمُ».
_source.english: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) said, ‘An Imam from among us can only be infallible. Infallibility is not an outward physical feature that can be noticed which is why it must be documented [in the Quran or traditions]. He was then asked, ‘O son of the Prophet, and what does infallible mean to which he replied, ‘It refers to one who clings fast to the rope of Allah, and the rope of Allah is the Quran. They do not separate from each other until the Day of Resurrection, and the Imam guides to the Quran and the Quran guides to the Imam, which is the purport of Allah s saying [in the Quran] “Verily this Quran guides to what is most upright”

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ لَمّا سَألَهُ هِشامٌ عَن مَعنَى المَعصومِ ـ: المَعصومُ هُوَ المُمتَنِعُ بِاللّهِ مِن جَميعِ مَحارِمِ اللّهِ ، وقالَ اللّهُ تَبارَكَ وتَعالى: «ومَن يَعتَصِمْ بِاللّهِ فقَد هُدِيَ إلى صِراطٍ مُستَقيمٍ»
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS), in reply to Hisham s question about the meaning of infallible, said, ‘The infallible [Imam] is prevented by Allah from all acts which Allah has prohibited, and Allah, Blessed and most High, says “And whoever takes recourse in Allah is certainly guided to a straight path”

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): إنَّ اللّهَ عزَّ ذِكرُهُ يَعصِمُ مَن أطاعَهُ، ولا يَعتَصِمُ بِهِ مَن عَصاهُ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘Verily Allah, Exalted be His remembrance, protects [from sin] whoever obeys Him, and whoever disobeys Him does not benefit from His protection.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): الاعِتبارُ يُثمِرُ العِصمَةَ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Drawing lessons [from past experiences] gives rise to sinlessness.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): إنَّ التَّقوى عِصمَةٌ لَكَ في حَياتِكَ ، وزُلفى لَكَ بَعدَ مَماتِكَ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Verily Godwariness is a protection [against sin] for you in your life, and a great profit for you after your death.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): بِالتَّقوى قُرِنَتِ العِصمَةُ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Sinlessness is fastened with Godwariness.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): الحِكمَةُ عِصمَةٌ ، العِصمَةُ نِعمَةٌ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Wisdom is sinlessness, and sinlessness is a bounty.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ في مُناجاتِهِ ـ: إلهي ، لا سَبيلَ إلى الاحتِراسِ مِنَ الذَّنبِ إلّا بِعِصمَتِكَ ، ولا وُصولَ إلى عَمَلِ الخَيراتِ إلّا بِمَشِيئَتِكَ ، فكَيفَ لي بِإفادَةِ ما أسلَفتَني فيهِ مَشيئَتَكَ ؟! وكَيفَ لي بِالاحتِراسِ مِنَ الذَّنبِ ما إن لَم تُدرِكْني فيهِ عِصمَتُكَ؟!
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said in his intimate supplication, ‘My God, I have no way to guard myself from sin except through Your protection, and no way to attain good deeds except by Your will. So how can I ever benefit from that which You have preceded with Your will! And how can I ever guard myself from sins as long as Your protection does not cover me therein!

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الباقرُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): إذا عَلِمَ اللّهُ تَعالى حُسنَ نِيَّةٍ مِن أحَدٍ اكتَنَفَهُ بِالعِصمَةِ .
_source.english: Imam al-Baqir (AS) said, ‘When Allah, most High, knows the good intention of a person, He encompasses him with His protection from all sides.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ في صِفَةِ الإمامِ ـ: مَعصوماً مِنَ الزَّلاّتِ ، مَصوناً عَنِ الفَواحِشِ كُلِّها .
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, describing the Imam, ‘He is immune from committing all errors, well-protected from all acts of indecency.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): نَحنُ تَراجِمَةُ أمرِ اللّهِ ، نَحنُ قَومٌ مَعصُومونَ.
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, ‘We are the interpreters of Allah s command, we are the infallible people.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الرِّضا (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): الإمامُ: المُطَهَّرُ مِنَ الذُّنوبِ ، والمُبَرَّأُ عَنِ العُيوبِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Rida (AS) said, ‘An Imam is purified from sins, immune from all flaws.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الرِّضا (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): . . . فهُوَ مَعصومٌ مُؤَيَّدٌ مُوَفَّقٌ مُسَدَّدٌ ، قَد أمِنَ مِنَ الخَطايا والزَّلَلِ والعِثارِ ، يَخُصُّهُ اللّهُ بِذلكَ لِيَكونَ حُجَّتَهُ عَلى عِبادِهِ وشاهِدَهُ عَلى خَلقِهِ .
_source.english: Imam al-Rida (AS) said, ‘He [i.e. the Imam] is therefore infallible, divinely supported, aided, and shielded; being immune from all mistakes, errors and lapses. Allah has endowed him that in order to make Him His proof on the servants and His witness over creation.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): الهِجرانُ عُقوبَةُ العِشقِ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Separation from one s beloved is the penalty for infatuation.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): ومَن عَشِقَ شَيئاً أعشى (أعمى) بَصَرَهُ وأمرَضَ قَلبَهُ ، فَهُوَ يَنظُرُ بِعَينٍ غَيرِ صَحيحَةٍ ، ويَسمَعُ بِاُذُنٍ غَيرِ سَميعَةٍ ، قَد خَرَقَتِ الشَّهَواتُ عَقلَهُ ، وأماتَتِ الدّنيا قَلبَهُ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The one who is infatuated with something, his eyes become blind and his heart becomes sick, such that he sees with unsound eyes and hears with deaf ears, his base desires having torn apart his reason and [love of] the world having killed his heart.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ لَمّا سُئلَ عَنِ العِشقِ ـ: قُلوبٌ خَلَت من ذِكرِ اللّهِ فأذاقَها اللّهُ حُبَّ غَيرِهِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS), when asked about infatuation, replied, ‘Hearts that are empty of the remembrance of Allah are given to taste by Allah the love of other than Him.

_source.chapter: The Reward for One Who Despite His Infatuation Restrains Himself
_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): مَن عَشِقَ فكَتَمَ وعَفَّ فماتَ فَهُوَ شَهيدٌ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘Whoever loves someone passionately, then suppresses his love in order to remain chaste and dies in the process, is a martyr.

_source.chapter: The Reward for One Who Despite His Infatuation Restrains Himself
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): ما المُجاهِدُ الشَّهيدُ في سَبيلِ اللّهِ بِأعظَمَ أجراً مِمَّن قَدَرَ فعَفَّ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The fighter who is martyred in the way of Allah has no greater reward than the one who is able to sate his lust but restrains himself.

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): يَقولُ اللّهُ عزَّوجلَّ: إذا كانَ الغالِبُ عَلَى العَبدِ الاشتِغالَ بي جَعَلتُ بُغيَتَهُ ولَذَّتَهُ في ذِكري ، فإذا جَعَلتُ بُغيَتَهُ ولَذَّتَهُ في ذِكري عَشِقَني وعَشِقتُهُ ، فإذا عَشِقَني وعَشِقتُهُ رَفَعتُ الحِجابَ فيما بَيني وبَينَهُ ، وصَيَّرتُ ذلكَ تَغالُبا عَلَيهِ ، لا يَسهو إذا سَها النّاسُ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘Allah, Mighty and Exalted, says, ‘When a servant s predominant state is preoccupation with Me then I make the object of his desire My remembrance and place his pleasure therein. And when I make My remembrance the object of his desire and place his pleasure therein, he becomes infatuated with Me and I with him. And when he becomes infatuated with Me and I with him, I remove all veils between Me and him, and make this state predominate over him where he is never again negligent even when other people are.

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): أفضَلُكُم إيماناً أفضَلُكُم مَعرِفَةً.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘The ones from among you with the best faith are the ones with the best inner knowledge.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): العِلمُ أوَّلُ دَليلٍ، والمَعرِفَةُ آخِرُ نِهايَةٍ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Knowledge is the first proof whereas inner knowledge is the last step in the conclusion.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): المَعرِفَةُ نورُ القَلبِ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Inner knowledge is the light of the heart.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الحسينُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): دِراسَةُ العِلمِ لِقاحُ المَعرِفةِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Husayn (AS) said, ‘The acquisition of knowledge is the seed for [the growth of] inner knowledge.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): لا يَقبَلُ اللّهُ عَمَلاً إلّا بِمَعرِفَةٍ، ولا مَعرِفَةً إلّا بِعَمَلٍ ، فمَن عَرَفَ دَلَّتهُ المَعرِفَةُ عَلَى العَمَلِ ، ومَن لَم يَعمَلْ فلا مَعرِفَةَ لَهُ .
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, ‘Allah does not accept any act without inner knowledge [i.e. awareness of what one is doing], and inner knowledge only comes through prior action. So whoever knows intrinsically, his knowledge will lead him to action, and whoever does not act does not have any inner knowledge.

_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): نورُ الحِكمَةِ الجُوعُ، والتَّباعُدُ مِنَ اللّهِ الشِّبَعُ ، والقُربَةُ إلَى اللّهِ حُبُّ المَساكينِ والدُّنُوُّ مِنهُم ، لا تَشبَعوا فَيُطفَأَ نورُ المَعرِفةِ مِن قُلوبِكُم.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘The light of inner knowledge is brought about by hunger whereas distance from Allah is caused by satiety. Proximity to Allah is brought about by loving the poor and drawing near to them, so do not eat to your fill lest the light of inner knowledge be extinguished from your hearts.

_source.chapter: The Inner Knowledge of the Self
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): مَعرِفَةُ النَّفسِ أنفَعُ المَعارِفِ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The inner knowledge of the self is the most beneficial of all such knowledge.

_source.chapter: The Inner Knowledge of the Self
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): نالَ الفَوزَ الأكبَرَ مَن ظَفِرَ بِمَعرِفَةِ النَّفسِ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The one who attains knowledge of his own self has obtained the greatest victory indeed.

_source.chapter: The Inner Knowledge of the Self
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): كَيفَ يَعرِفُ غَيرَهُ مَن يَجهَلُ نَفسَهُ؟!
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘How can one who is ignorant of his own self expect to know others?!

_source.chapter: The Inner Knowledge of the Self
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): مَن عَرَفَ نَفسَهُ جاهَدَها ، مَن جَهِلَ نَفسَهُ أهمَلَها .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘He who gains inner knowledge of his self combats it, and he who remains ignorant of his self, neglects it.

_source.chapter: The Inner Knowledge of the Self
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): مَن عَرَفَ اللّهَ تَوَحَّدَ ، مَن عَرَفَ نَفسَهُ تَجَرَّدَ ، مَن عَرَفَ الدّنيا تَزَهَّدَ ، مَن عَرَفَ النّاسَ تَفَرَّدَ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘He who attains inner knowledge of Allah leads a life of unity [reflecting Allahs Divine Unity]; he who attains inner knowledge of his self strips himself [of all that hinders its progress]; he who attains inner knowledge about this world abstains from it; and he who attains inner knowledge about people prefers solitude.

_source.chapter: The Inner Knowledge of the Self
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): أكثَرُ النّاسِ مَعرِفَةً لِنَفسِهِ أخوَفُهُم لِرَبِّهِ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The person who knows his self the best is he who fears his Lord the most.

_source.chapter: The Inner Knowledge of the Self
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): مَن عَرَفَ نَفسَهُ عَرَفَ رَبَّهُ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘He who attains inner knowledge of his self attains inner knowledge of his Lord.

_source.chapter: The Inner Knowledge of the Self
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): يَنبَغي لِمَن عَلِمَ شَرَفَ نَفسِهِ أن يُنَزِّهَها عَن دَناءَةِ الدّنيا .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘It befits one who knows the dignity of his own self to deem it too great for the vileness of this world.

_source.chapter: The Inner Knowledge of the Self
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): يَنبَغي لِمَن عَرَفَ نَفسَهُ أن يَلزَمَ القَناعَةَ والعِفَّةَ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘It befits one who knows the dignity of his own self to adhere to temperance and self-restraint.

_source.chapter: The Inner Knowledge of the Self
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): يَنبَغي لِمَن عَرَفَ نَفسَهُ أن لا يُفارِقَهُ الحُزنُ والحَذَرُ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘It befits one who knows the dignity of his own self to never allow a sorrowful and self-cautious state to leave him.

_source.chapter: The Inner Knowledge of the Self
_source.arabic: الإمامُ زينَ العابدينُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ في الدُّعاءِ ـ: واجعَلنا مِنَ الّذين عَرَفوا أنفُسَهُم ، وأيقَنوا بِمُستَقَرِّهِم ، فكانَت أعمارُهُم في طاعَتِكَ تَفنى.
_source.english: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) said in one of his supplications, ‘Make us from among those who have attained inner knowledge of their selves and are convinced of their true abode, such that they spend their whole lives in Your obedience.

_source.chapter: The Inner Knowledge of the Self
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الباقرُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ في وَصِيَّتِهِ لِجابِرٍ الجُعفيِّ ـ: لا مَعرِفةَ كَمَعرِفَتِكَ بِنَفسِكَ.
_source.english: Imam al-Baqir (AS) said in his advice to Jabir al-Juafi, ‘There is no inner knowledge like your inner knowledge of your own self.

_source.chapter: The Virtue of Attaining Inner Knowledge of Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): مَن عَرَفَ اللّهَ كَمُلَت مَعرِفتُهُ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘He who attains inner knowledge of Allah has achieved perfection in his knowledge indeed.

_source.chapter: The Virtue of Attaining Inner Knowledge of Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): مَعرِفةُ اللّهِ سُبحانَهُ أعلى المَعارِفِ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The inner knowledge of Allah, Glory be to Him, is the highest of knowable truths.

_source.chapter: The Virtue of Attaining Inner Knowledge of Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): ما يَسُرُّني لَو مِتُّ طِفلاً واُدخِلتُ الجَنَّةَ ولم أكبُرْ فأعرِفَ رَبّي عَزَّوجلَّ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘I would not be pleased to die as a child and be made to enter Paradise without being able to grow up and get to know my Lord, Mighty and Exalted.

_source.chapter: The Virtue of Attaining Inner Knowledge of Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): ثَمَرَةُ العِلمِ مَعرِفَةُ اللّهِ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The fruit of knowledge is attaining inner knowledge of Allah.

_source.chapter: The Virtue of Attaining Inner Knowledge of Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): مَن سَكَنَ قَلبَهُ العِلمُ بِاللّهِ سَكَنَهُ الغِنى عَن خَلقِ اللّهِ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘He whose heart finds peace in knowing Allah, finds peace in being needless of Allahs creatures.

_source.chapter: The Virtue of Attaining Inner Knowledge of Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): لَو يَعلَمُ النّاسُ ما في فَضلِ مَعرِفةِ اللّهِ عَزَّوجلَّ ما مَدُّوا أعيُنَهُم إلى ما مَتَّعَ اللّهُ بِهِ الأعداءَ مِن زَهرَةِ الحَياةِ الدّنيا ونَعيمِها ، وكانَت دُنياهُم أقَلَّ عِندَهُم مِمّا يَطَؤونَهُ بِأرجُلِهِم، ولَنَعِموا بِمَعرِفةِ اللّهِ جَلَّ وعزَّ ، وتَلَذَّذوا بِها تَلَذُّذَ مَن لَم يَزَلْ في رَوضاتِ الجِنانِ مَعَ أولِياءِ اللّهِ . إنَّ مَعرِفةَ اللّهِ عَزَّوجلَّ اُنسٌ مِن كُلِّ وَحشَةٍ ، وصاحِبٌ مِن كُلِّ وَحدَةٍ ، ونُورٌ مِن كُلِّ ظُلمَةٍ ، وقُوَّةٌ مِن كُلِّ ضَعفٍ ، وشِفاءٌ مِن كُلِّ سُقمٍ .
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, ‘If people knew the virtue of knowing Allah, Mighty and Exalted, they would never extend their gaze to the splendour and bounties of the life of this world that Allah has granted to the enemies. They would then regard such peoples worldly goods to be more insignificant that the dust under their feet, and they would take great pleasure at attaining knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Exalted, and would savour it as if they were tasting the experience of being in the gardens of Paradise with the friends of Allah. Verily the inner knowledge of Allah is an intimate companion in every type of desolation, a friend in every type of loneliness, a light in every darkness, a source of strength from all weakness, and a cure for all ailments.

_source.chapter: The Fruits of Inner Knowledge of Allah
_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): مَن عَرَفَ اللّهَ وعَظَّمَهُ مَنَعَ فاهُ مِنَ الكَلامِ وبَطنَهُ مِنَ الطَّعامِ ، وعَنّى نَفسَهُ بِالصِّيامِ والقِيامِ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘He who attains inner knowledge of Allah and aggrandizes Him forbids his mouth from speaking [vain] and his stomach from eating, and satisfies himself through fasting and praying.

_source.chapter: The Fruits of Inner Knowledge of Allah
_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): لَو عَرَفتُمُ اللّهَ حَقَّ مَعرِفتِهِ لَمَشَيتُم عَلَى البُحورِ ، ولَزالَت بِدُعائكُمُ الجِبالُ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘If you truly knew Allah as He is worthy of being known, you would be able to walk on the seas and the mountains would fall by your command.

_source.chapter: The Fruits of Inner Knowledge of Allah
_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): مَن كانَ بِاللّهِ أعرَفَ كانَ مِنَ اللّهِ أخوَفَ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘He who is most knowledgeable of Allah is most fearful of Allah.

_source.chapter: The Fruits of Inner Knowledge of Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): يَسيرُ المَعرِفَةِ يُوجِبُ الزُّهدَ في الدّنيا.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The least knowledge of Allah leads one to abstain from the vanities of this world.

_source.chapter: The Fruits of Inner Knowledge of Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): إِنَّهُ لا يَنبَغي لِمَن عَرَفَ عَظَمَةَ اللّهِ أن يَتَعَظَّمَ ؛ فإنَّ رِفعَةَ الّذينَ يَعلَمونَ ما عَظَمَتُهُ أن يَتَواضَعوا لَهُ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Verily it does not befit one who has attained inner knowledge of the grandeur of Allah to behave proudly, for verily the elevation of those who acknowledge His grandeur comes from their abasing themselves in front of Him.

_source.chapter: The Fruits of Inner Knowledge of Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): غايَةُ المَعرِفَةِ الخَشيَةُ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The peak of inner knowledge of Allah is fear [of Him].

_source.chapter: The Fruits of Inner Knowledge of Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): أعلَمُ النّاسِ بِاللّهِ أكثَرُهُم لَهُ مَسألَةً .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The person who best knows Allah asks of Him the most.

_source.chapter: The Fruits of Inner Knowledge of Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الباقرُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): أحَقُّ خَلقِ اللّهِ أن يُسَلِّمَ لِما قَضَى اللّهُ عَزَّوجلَّ: مَن عَرَفَ اللّهَ عَزَّوجلَّ.
_source.english: Imam al-Baqir (AS) said, ‘The creature of Allah most eligible for submission to the decree of Allah, Mighty and Exalted, is he who knows Allah, Mighty and Exalted.

_source.chapter: The Fruits of Inner Knowledge of Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): مَن عَرَفَ اللّهَ خافَ اللّهَ ، ومَن خافَ اللّهَ سَخَت نَفسُهُ عَنِ الدّنيا .
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, ‘He who attains inner knowledge of Allah fears Allah, and he who fears Allah restrains himself from this world.

_source.chapter: The Fruits of Inner Knowledge of Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): إنَّ أعلَمَ النّاسِ بِاللّهِ أرضاهُم بِقَضاءِ اللّهِ عَزَّوجلَّ .
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, ‘Verily the person who best knows Allah is the most content with the decree of Allah, Mighty and Exalted.'

_source.chapter: The Description of the One who Knows Allah [or the Gnostic]
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): العارِفُ وَجهُهُ مُستَبشِرٌ مُتَبَسِّمٌ ، وقَلبُهُ وَجِلٌ مَحزونٌ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The gnostics face is cheerful and smily, whereas his heart is apprehensive and sorrowful.

_source.chapter: The Description of the One who Knows Allah [or the Gnostic]
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): الشَّوقُ خُلصانُ العارِفينَ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Longing [for Allah] is the sincerest friend of the gnostics.

_source.chapter: The Description of the One who Knows Allah [or the Gnostic]
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): الخَوفُ جِلبابُ العارِفينَ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Fear is the cloak of the gnostics.

_source.chapter: The Description of the One who Knows Allah [or the Gnostic]
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): البُكاءُ مِن خِيفَةِ اللّهِ لِلبُعدِ عَنِ اللّهِ عِبادَةُ العارِفينَ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Crying much due to fear of Allah for any possible distance between oneself and Allah is the regular worshipful state of the gnostics.

_source.chapter: The Description of the One who Knows Allah [or the Gnostic]
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): ثِقْ بِاللّهِ تَكُن عارِفاً.
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, ‘Trust in Allah and you will attain inner knowledge [of Him].

_source.chapter: The Lowest Degree of Inner Knowledge
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الكاظمُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ لَمّا سُئلَ عَن أدنَى المَعرِفةِ ـ: الإقرارُ بأنَّهُ لا إلهَ غَيرُهُ ، ولا شِبهَ لَهُ ولا نَظيرَ وأنَّهُ قَديمٌ ، مُثبَتٌ ، مَوجودٌ ، غَيرُ فَقيدٍ ، وأنَّهُ لَيسَ كَمِثلِه شَيءٌ .
_source.english: Imam al-Kazim (AS), when he was asked about the lowest degree of inner knowledge, replied, ‘It is to affirm that there is no god but He, and that He has no likeness or match, and that He is eternal, positively proven to exist, present and not absent, and that there is nothing like Him.

_source.chapter: Attaining Inner Knowledge of Allah Through Allah Himself
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): اِعرِفوا اللّهَ بِاللّهِ ، والرَّسولَ بِالرِّسالَةِ ، واُولي الأمرِ بِالأمرِ بِالمَعروفِ والعَدلِ والإحسانِ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Get to know Allah through Allah, and the Prophet through the message he brought, and those vested with authority through their command to do good, their justice and righteousness.

_source.chapter: Attaining Inner Knowledge of Allah Through Allah Himself
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الحسينُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ في الدُّعاءِ ـ: إلهي تَرَدُّدي في الآثارِ يُوجِبُ بُعدَ المَزارِ ، فاجمَعْني عَلَيكَ بِخِدمَةٍ تُوصِلُني إلَيكَ ، كَيفَ يُستَدَلُّ عَلَيكَ بِما هُوَ في وُجودِهِ مُفتَقِرٌ إلَيكَ؟! أيَكونُ لِغَيرِكَ مِنَ الظُّهورِ ما لَيسَ لَكَ حتّى يَكونَ هُوَ المُظهِرَ لَكَ ؟! متى غِبتَ حتّى تَحتاجَ إلى دَليلٍ يَدُلُّ عَلَيكَ؟! ... بِكَ أستَدِلُّ عَلَيكَ فَاهْدِني بِنورِكَ إلَيكَ.
_source.english: Imam al-Husayn (AS) said in one of his supplications, ‘My God! My own obscure doubts about the signs [in nature] has caused my distance from my goal, so draw me near to You through Your service that may allow me to reach You. How can something that needs You for its very existence be used to prove Your existence?! Are other things more manifest than You that they be used to point to You?! When were You ever absent that You should need anything to prove Your existence?! Through You alone do I arrive at You, so guide me with Your light to Yourself.

_source.chapter: Attaining Inner Knowledge of Allah Through Allah Himself
_source.arabic: الإمامِ زينِ العابدينَ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ في الدّعاءِ ـ: بِكَ عَرَفتُكَ و أنتَ دَلَلتَني عَلَيكَ و دَعَوتَني إلَيكَ ، و لَولا أنتَ لَم أدرِ ما أنتَ.
_source.english: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) said in one of his supplications, ‘I have attained knowledge of You through You, and You are the One Who indicated me to Yourself and called me to Yourself, and were it not for You, I would not know who You are.

_source.chapter: Prohibition of Pondering About Allahs Essence
_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): تَفَكَّروا في خَلقِ اللّهِ ، ولا تَفَكَّروا في اللّهِ فتَهلِكوا.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘Ponder about the creation of Allah, but do not ponder about Allah Himself lest you be ruined.
_source.chapter_ar: النَّهيُ عَنِ التَّفَكُّرِ في ذاتِ اللّهِ

_source.chapter: Prohibition of Pondering About Allahs Essence
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): إيّاكُم والتَّفَكُّرَ في اللّهِ؛ فإنَّ التَّفَكُّرَ في اللّهِ لا يَزيدُ إلّا تِيهاً ، إنَّ اللّهَ عَزَّوجلَّ لا تُدرِكُهُ الأبصارُ ولا يُوصَفُ بِمِقدارٍ.
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, ‘Beware of pondering about Allah, for verily pondering about Allah only increases ones bewilderment. Verily Allah, Mighty and Exalted, cannot be perceived by the sights or described by any type of criteria.
_source.chapter_ar: النَّهيُ عَنِ التَّفَكُّرِ في ذاتِ اللّهِ

_source.chapter: Prohibition of Pondering About Allahs Essence
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): مَن نَظَرَ في اللّهِ كَيفَ هُوَ هَلَكَ.
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, ‘How ruined is the one who examines Allah!'
_source.chapter_ar: النَّهيُ عَنِ التَّفَكُّرِ في ذاتِ اللّهِ

_source.chapter: The Intellects Incapacity to Fathom His Essence
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): فلَسنا نَعلَمُ كُنهَ عَظَمَتِكَ، إلّا أنّا نَعلَمُ أنَّكَ حَيٌّ قَيّومٌ ، لا تَأخُذُكَ سِنَةٌ ولا نَومٌ ، لَم يَنتَهِ إلَيكَ نَظَرٌ ، ولَم يُدرِكْكَ بَصَرٌ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘We do not know the essence of Your greatness. All that we do know is that You are Ever-Living and Self-Subsisting through Whom all things subsist. Drowsiness and sleep do not overtake You, vision does not reach You and sight cannot perceive You.

_source.chapter: The Intellects Incapacity to Fathom His Essence
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ في صِفَةِ المَلائكَةِ ـ: وإنَّهُم عَلى مَكانِهِم مِنكَ ، ومَنزِلَتِهِم عِندَكَ، واستِجماعِ أهوائهِم فيكَ ، وكَثرَةِ طاعَتِهِم لَكَ ، وقِلَّةِ غَفلَتِهِم عَن أمرِكَ ، لَو عايَنوا كُنهَ ما خَفِيَ عَلَيهِم مِنكَ لَحَقَّروا أعمالَهُم ، ولَزَرَوا عَلى أنفُسِهِم ، ولَعَرَفوا أنَّهُم لَم يَعبُدوكَ حَقَّ عِبادَتِكَ ، ولَم يُطيعوكَ حَقَّ طاعَتِكَ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said in his description of the angels, ‘They are in their own places [distinct] from You, [and yet] their positions are near You. Their desires are all concentrated on You, their worship for You is abundant, and their neglect of Your command is little. If they were to witness the essence of what is hidden about You from them, they would regard their deeds insignificant, they would reproach themselves and would realize that they have not worshipped You as You deserve to be worshipped, and have not obeyed You as You deserve to be obeyed.

_source.chapter: The Intellects Incapacity to Fathom His Essence
_source.arabic: الإمام زينُ العابدينَ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ في الدّعاءِ ـ: عَجَزَتِ العُقولُ عَن إدراكِ كُنهِ جَمالِكَ ، وانحَسَرَتِ الأبصارُ دونَ النَّظَرِ إلى سُبُحاتِ وَجهِكَ، ولَم تَجعَلْ لِلخَلقِ طَريقا إلى مَعرِفَتِكَ إلّا بِالعَجزِ عَن مَعرِفَتِكَ .
_source.english: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) said in one of his supplications, ‘The intellects are incapable of fathoming the essence of Your Beauty, the sights are restricted to looking at other than the splendour of Your Countenance, and You have not set aside any means for Your creation to get to know You except through their complete incapacity of knowing You.

_source.chapter: The Intellects Incapacity to Fathom His Essence
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الرِّضا (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): كُنهُهُ تَفريقٌ بَينَهُ وبَينَ خَلقِهِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Rida (AS) said, ‘His essence is a partition between Himself and His creation.

_source.chapter: The Intellects Incapacity to Fathom His Essence
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الرِّضا (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ في صِفَةِ اللّهِ سُبحانَهُ ـ: هُوَ أجَلُّ مِن أن يُدرِكَهُ بَصَرٌ ، أو يُحيطَ بِه وَهمٌ ، أو يَضبِطَهُ عَقلٌ.
_source.english: Imam al-Rida (AS) said in his description of Allah, Glory be to Him, ‘He is too exalted for sight to be able to perceive Him, for imagination to be able to fathom Him, and for the intellect to be able to grasp Him.

_source.chapter: The Extent to Which One is Allowed to Describe Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): مَن وَصَفَهُ فَقَد حَدَّهُ ، ومَن حَدَّهُ فَقَد عَدَّهُ ، ومَن عَدَّهُ فَقَد أبطَلَ أزَلَهُ ، ومَن قالَ: «كَيفَ ؟» فقَدِ استَوصَفَهُ ، ومَن قالَ: «أينَ ؟» فقَد حَيَّزَهُ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘He who [undertakes to] describe Him has defined Him, and he who defines Him has numbered Him, and he who numbers Him has nullified His eternity. He who asks ‘How? [about Allah] has indeed sought to describe Him, and he who asks ‘Where? has indeed confined Him.

_source.chapter: The Extent to Which One is Allowed to Describe Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): فتَبارَكَ اللّهُ الّذي لا يَبلُغُهُ بُعدُ الهِمَمِ ، ولا يَنالُهُ حَدسُ الفِطَنِ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘So blessed be the One Whom the highest ambitions cannot reach and Whom the conjecture of intelligent minds cannot grasp.

_source.chapter: The Extent to Which One is Allowed to Describe Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): واحِدٌ لا بِعَدَدٍ ، ودائمٌ لا بِأمَدٍ، وقائمٌ لا بِعَمَدٍ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘[He is] One, but not by enumeration. He is everlasting without extremity. He exists without any support.

_source.chapter: The Extent to Which One is Allowed to Describe Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامِ الصّادقِ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): قالَ رجلٌ عندهُ: اللّهُ أكبَرُ، فقالَ: اللّهُ أكبَرُ مِن أيِّ شَيءٍ ؟ فقالَ: مِن كُلِّ شَيءٍ ، فقالَ أبو عَبدِ اللّهِ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): حَدَّدتَهُ، فقالَ الرَّجُلُ: كَيفَ أقولُ ؟ قالَ: قُل: اللّهُ أكبَرُ مِن أن يُوصَفَ .
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) asked a man who said ‘Allah is Greater (Allahu Akbar), ‘Greater than what? So the man replied, ‘Greater than everything, to which Imam (AS) retorted, ‘Then you have defined Him. The man then asked him, ‘So what should I say? Imam replied, ‘Say: Allah is too great for description.

_source.chapter: The Extent to Which One is Allowed to Describe Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الكاظمُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): إنَّ اللّهَ أعلى وأجَلُّ وأعظَمُ مِن أن يُبلَغَ كُنهُ صِفَتِهِ ، فَصِفُوهُ بِما وَصَفَ بِهِ نَفسَهُ ، وكُفّوا عَمّا سِوى ذلكَ .
_source.english: Imam al-Kazim (AS) said, ‘Verily Allah is too High and too Exalted and too Great for the reality of His description to ever be possible, so describe Him as He Himself has described Himself, and desist from anything other than that.

_source.chapter: The Extent to Which One is Allowed to Describe Allah
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الهاديُّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): إنّ الخالِقَ لا يُوصَفُ إلّا بِما وَصَفَ بِهِ نَفسَهُ ، وأنّى يُوصَفُ الخالِقُ الّذي تَعجُزُ الحَواسُّ أن تُدرِكَهُ، والأوهامُ أن تَنالَهُ ، والخَطَراتُ أن تَحُدَّهُ ، والأبصارُ عَنِ الإحاطَةِ بِهِ؟! جلَّ عَمّا يَصِفُهُ الواصِفونَ ، وتَعالى عَمّا يَنعَتُهُ الناعِتونَ.
_source.english: Imam al-Hadi (AS) said, ‘Verily the Creator can only be described by that which He Himself has described Himself, and how can the Creator ever be described anyway, Whom the senses are incapable of perceiving and the imaginations unable to grasp and the ideas unable to confine and the sights unable to contain?! He is too exalted for the description of those who undertake to describe, and too high to be attributed by those who seek to attach attributes to Him.

_source.chapter: [Faith and Inner Knowledge of] The Divine Unity of Allah (tawhid)
_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): التَّوحيدُ نِصفُ الدِّينِ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘Allahs divine Unity is half of religion.
_source.cited_from: Uyoun Akhbar al-Ridha (AS), volume:2, p. 35, number:75

_source.chapter: [Faith and Inner Knowledge of] The Divine Unity of Allah (tawhid)
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): التَّوحيدُ حَياةُ النَّفسِ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Allahs divine Unity is the life of the soul.

_source.chapter: [Faith and Inner Knowledge of] The Divine Unity of Allah (tawhid)
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): التَّوحيدُ إلّا تَتَوَهَّمَهُ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘[Faith in] Allahs divine Unity is that you do not subject Him to the limitations of your imagination.

_source.chapter: [Faith and Inner Knowledge of] The Divine Unity of Allah (tawhid)
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ لِرَجُلٍ ـ: أمَّا التَّوحيدُ فأن لا تُجوِّزَ عَلى رَبِّكَ ما جازَ عَلَيكَ ، وأمَّا العَدلُ فأن لا تَنسِبَ إلى خالِقِكَ ما لامَكَ عَلَيهِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, ‘[Faith in] Allahs divine Unity is that you do not deem applicable to your Lord that which applies to you, and [faith in] His divine Justice is that you do not blame Him for that which you are blameworthy.

_source.chapter: [Faith and Inner Knowledge of] The Divine Unity of Allah (tawhid)
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الرِّضا (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): أوَّلُ عِبادَةِ اللّهِ مَعرِفتُهُ، وأصلُ مَعرِفةِ اللّهِ جلَّ اسمُهُ تَوحيدُهُ ، ونِظامُ تَوحيدِهِ نَفيُ التَّحديدِ عَنهُ ؛ لِشَهادَةِ العُقولِ أنَّ كلَّ مَحدودٍ مَخلوقٌ .
_source.english: Imam al-Rida (AS) said, ‘The very first step to Allahs worship is to attain inner knowledge of Him, and the origin of attaining inner knowledge of Allah, Exalted be His Praise, is through His divine Unity. The very basis of His divine Unity is to negate any kind of limitation from Him, since the intellects are able to witness that every limited being is created.

_source.chapter: The Proof of Allahs Divine Unity
_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ في وَصِيَّتِه لاِبنِه الحَسَنِ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ: واعلَمْ يا بُنَيَّ أنَّهُ لَو كانَ لِرَبِّكَ شَريكٌ لَأتَتكَ رُسُلُهُ ، ولَرَأيتَ آثارَ مُلكِهِ وسُلطانِهِ ، ولَعَرَفتَ أفعالَهُ وصِفاتِهِ، ولكِنَّهُ إلهٌ واحِدٌ كَما وَصَفَ نَفسَهُ ، لا يُضادُّهُ في مُلكِهِ أحَدٌ ، ولا يَزولُ أبَداً.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said in his will to his son, al-Hasan (AS), ‘And know my son that if your Lord were to have a partner, his messengers would surely have come to you, and you would have seen the signs of his dominion and his power, and you would know his acts and his attributes. He, however, is One God, just as He as described Himself. He is neither opposed by anyone in His kingdom, nor will He ever cease to be.

_source.chapter: The Proof of Allahs Divine Unity
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ مِن مُناظَرَتِهِ زِندِيقا ـ: إن قُلتَ: إنَّهُما اثنانِ لَم يَخْلُ مِن أن يَكونا مُتَّفِقَينِ مِن كُلِّ جِهَةٍ ، أو مُفتَرِقَينِ مِن كُلِّ جِهَةٍ ، فلَمّا رَأينا الخَلقَ مُنتَظِماً، والفَلَكَ جارِياً، واختلافَ اللَّيلِ والنَّهارِ، والشَّمسِ والقَمَرِ ، دَلَّ صِحَّةُ الأمرِ والتَّدبيرِ وائتِلافُ الأمرِ عَلى أنَّ المُدَبِّرَ واحِدٌ. ثُمّ يَلزَمُكَ إنِ ادَّعَيتَ اثنَينِ فلابُدَّ مِن فُرجَةٍ بَينَهُما حتّى يَكونا اثنَينِ ، فصارَتِ الفُرجَةُ ثالِثاً بَينَهُما قَديماً مَعَهُما فيَلزَمُكَ ثَلاثَةٌ، فإنِ ادَّعيتَ ثَلاثَةً لَزِمَكَ ما قُلنا في الاثنَينِ حتّى يَكونَ بَينَهُم فُرجَتانِ فيَكونَ خَمساً، ثُمّ يَتَناهى في العَدَدِ إلى ما لا نِهايَةَ في الكَثرَةِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS), when he was debating with an atheist, said, ‘If you say that there are two gods, then they are either in complete agreement on everything or completely separate in their spheres of influence. But when we look at this orderly creation, the continuous orbits, the alternation of night and day, and the sun and the moon, the soundness of the situation and the organisation and sound management of it indicates that the Director [of all creation] is One. Then if you still claim that there are two gods, then there must necessarily be some kind of difference between them for them to be two [and therefore distinct from each other], and this distinguishing characteristic between them is itself eternal like them, so you are forced to accept three such beings. And if you hold that there are indeed three, then you have to admit the same thing that we said for two such that they [the three] necessarily have two distinguishing characteristics between them [to differentiate them from each other] so then there are five [such eternal beings] altogether, and thus does the multiplication continue until infinity.

_source.chapter: The Proof of Allahs Divine Unity
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ لَمّا سُئلَ عَنِ الدَّليلِ عَلى أنَّ اللّهَ واحِدٌ ـ: اتِّصالُ التَّدبيرِ، وتَمامُ الصُّنعِ ، كَما قالَ اللّهُ عَزَّوجلَّ: «لَو كانَ فيهِما آلِهَةٌ إلّا اللّهُ لَفَسَدَتا»
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS), when asked to give proof that Allah is One, said, ‘The continuous unity of management [in the cosmos] and the perfection of creation, as Allah, Mighty and Exalted, has said, “Had there been gods in them (i.e. the heavens and the earth) other than Allah, they would surely have fallen apart”

_source.chapter: The Proof of Allahs Divine Unity
_source.arabic: الإمامِ الرِّضا (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ لَمّا سألَهُ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الثَنَوِيَّةِ: إنّي أقولُ: إنّ صانِعَ العالَمِ اثنانِ ، فما الدَّليلُ عَلى أنَّهُ واحِدٌ؟ ـ: قَولُكَ: إنَّهُ اثنانِ دَليلٌ عَلى أنَّهُ واحِدٌ ؛ لِأنَّكَ لَم تَدَّعِ الثّانِيَ إلّا بَعدَ إثباتِكَ الواحِدَ ، فالواحِدُ مُجمَعٌ عَلَيهِ ، وأكثَرُ مِن واحِدٍ مُختَلَفٌ فيهِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Rida (AS) was asked the following by a man believing in dualism, ‘I believe that the creator of the world are two, so what is the proof that He is One? Imam replied, ‘Your belief that there are two is proof in itself that He is One, for verily you have only claimed the second after having affirmed the existence of the One. So the One is already a unanimous fact it is more than one that is controversial [and remains to be proven.

_source.chapter: The Proof of Allahs Divine Unity
_source.arabic: تفسير القمّي: ثُمّ رَدَّ اللّهُ عَلَى الثَّنَويَّةِ الّذينَ قالوا بِإلهَينِ فقالَ اللّهُ تَعالى: «ما اتَّخَذَ اللّهُ مِن وَلَدٍ وما كانَ مَعَهُ مِن إلهٍ ...» قالَ: لَو كانا إلهَينِ كَما زَعَمتُم لَكانا يَختِلفان ؛ فيَخلُقُ هذا ولا يَخلُقُ هذا، ويُريدُ هذا ولا يُريدُ هذا، ويَطلبُ كلُّ واحدٍ مِنهما الغَلَبَةَ، وإذا أرادَ أحدُهُما خَلْقَ إنسانٍ أرادَ الآخرُ خَلْقَ بَهيمَةٍ، فيكونُ إنساناً وبَهيمةً في حالَةٍ واحِدَةٍ ، وهذا غيرُ مَوجودٍ، فَلَمّا بَطُلَ هذا ثَبَتَ التَّدبيرُ والصِنعُ لِواحدٍ، ودَلَّ أيضا التَّدبيرُ وثباتُهُ وقِوامُ بَعضِهِ بِبَعضٍ على أنَّ الصّانِعَ واحدٌ وذلكَ قَولُهُ: «ما اتَّخَذَ اللّهُ مِن وَلَدٍ»إلى قَولِهِ: «لَعَلا بَعْضُهُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ».
_source.english: It is written in Tafsir al-Qummi: ‘Then Allah, Mighty and Exalted, answered dualism and those who professed that there were two gods, saying: “Allah has not taken any offspring, neither is there any god besides Him, for then each god would take away what he created, and some of them would surely rise up against others. Clear is Allah of what they allege!” Quran 23:91 If there were two gods, as you claim, each one of them would seek superiority, and if one of them desired to create a man, the other would desire to oppose him and create an animal, so their joint creation would have to be the product of both their desires, in spite of their differing wills, man and beast at the same time. And this is the most impossible thing that does not even exist. And if this argument is invalid and there is no difference between them, then the whole duality is invalid [with no distinction left between the two and there is only one. Therefore, this order, unity of arrangement, subsistence of some things through other things, all indicate to One Maker, and this is the purport of Allahs verse in the Quran: “Allah has not taken any offspring neither is there any god besides Him…” and “Had there been gods in them (i.e. the heavens and the earth) other than Allah, they would surely have fallen apart.”

_source.chapter: The Sights Cannot Apprehend Him but The Hearts Behold Him
_source.arabic: رسولُ اللهِ (صَلَّيَ اللهُ عَلَيهِ وَ آلِهِ): لَمّا اُسرِيَ بي إلَى السَّماءِ بَلَغَ بي جَبرَئيلُ مَكاناً لَم يَطَأْهُ جَبرئيلُ قَطُّ ، فكُشِفَ لي فأرانِيَ اللّهُ عَزَّوجلَّ مِن نورِ عَظَمَتِهِ ما أحَبَّ.
_source.english: The Prophet (SAWA) said, ‘When I was taken on my Night Journey to the heavens, Gabriel took me up until a place wherein he himself had never set foot. The veils were pulled away for me and Allah, Mighty and Exalted, showed me whatever He liked from the light of His Greatness.

_source.chapter: The Sights Cannot Apprehend Him but The Hearts Behold Him
_source.arabic: لَمّا جَلَسَ عَليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) فِي الخِلافَةِ ... فَقامَ إلَيهِ رَجلٌ يقالُ لهُ ذعلب ... فقالَ: يا أميرَ المؤمنينَ، هَلْ رأيتَ رَبَّكَ؟ فَقالَ: وَيلَكَ يا ذَعلَبُ! لَم أكُن بِالّذي أعبُدُ رَبّاً لَم أرَهُ ! قالَ: فكَيفَ رَأيتَهُ ؟ صِفْهُ لَنا؟ قالَ: وَيلَكَ! لَم تَرَهُ العُيونُ بِمُشاهَدَةِ الأبصارِ، ولكِنْ رَأتهُ القُلوبُ بِحَقائقِ الإيمانِ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said in reply to Dhaalabs question about his being able to see his Lord, ‘Woe to you O Dhaalab! I do not worship a Lord Whom I cannot see! So Dhaalab asked, ‘But how do you see Him? Describe Him to us. Imam (AS) replied, ‘Woe betide you! Eyes do not see Him by looking with the sights; it is the hearts that behold Him with the realities of faith.

_source.chapter: The Sights Cannot Apprehend Him but The Hearts Behold Him
_source.arabic: الإمامُ الرِّضا (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ في قولِهِ تعالى: «لا تُدرِكُهُ الأبصارُ ...» ـ: لا تُدرِكُهُ أوهامُ القُلوبِ ، فكَيفَ تُدرِكُهُ أبصارُ العُيونِ؟!
_source.english: Imam al-Rida (AS), with regards to Allahs verse in the Quran: “The sights do not apprehend Him…” said, ‘The hearts fancies cannot apprehend Him so how can the eyesights apprehend Him?!

_source.chapter: The Sights Cannot Apprehend Him but The Hearts Behold Him
_source.arabic: الإمامُ العسكريُّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): إنَّ اللّهَ تَبارَكَ وتَعالى أرى رَسولَهُ بِقَلبِهِ مِن نورِ عَظَمَتِهِ ما أحَبَّ.
_source.english: Imam al-Aaskari (AS) said, ‘Verily Allah, Blessed and most High, displayed to His Prophet in his heart, whatever He liked from the light of His Greatness.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): الحَمدُ للّهِ الأوَّلِ قَبلَ كُلِّ أوَّلٍ ، والآخِرِ بَعدَ كُلِّ آخِرٍ ، وبِأوَّلِيَّتِهِ وَجَبَ أن لا أوَّلَ لَهُ ، وبآخِرِيَّتِهِ وَجَبَ أن لا آخِرَ لَهُ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Praise be to Allah, the First before every first, and the Last after every last, and His Firstness necessitates that there is no beginning to Him, and His Lastness necessitates that there is no end to Him.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): لا يَزولُ أبَداً ولَم يَزَلْ، أوَّلٌ قَبلَ الأشياءِ بِلا أوَّلِيَّةٍ ، وآخِرٌ بَعدَ الأشياءِ بِلا نِهايَةٍ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘He never ceases to exist and will always be, the First before all things without a beginning, and the Last after all things without an end.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ وقَد سَألَهُ رَجُلٌ يَهودِيٌّ: مَتى كانَ رَبُّنا عَزَّوجلَّ؟ ـ: يا يَهودِيُّ ، (ما كانَ) لَم يَكُنْ رَبُّنا فكانَ ، وإنَّما يُقالُ: «مَتى كانَ» لِشَيءٍ لَم يَكُنْ فكانَ ، هُوَ كائنٌ بِلا كَينونَةِ كائنٍ لَم يَزَلْ لَيسَ لَهُ قَبلٌ ، هُوَ قَبلَ القَبلِ ، وقَبلَ الغايَةِ ، انقَطَعَتْ عَنهُ الغاياتُ ، فهُوَ غايَةُ كُلِّ غايَةٍ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) was once asked by a Jew, ‘When did our Lord, Mighty and Exalted, come to be?, to which he replied, ‘O Jew, It is not that our Lord was not and then came to be, for the question ‘When did x come to be? is posed regarding something that is not there and then comes to be. He exists without coming into being; He is ever existing having nothing before Him. He is before ‘before itself, before any limit. Limits do not apply to Him for He is the ultimate limit of all limits.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الباقرُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): إنَّ اللّهَ تَبارَكَ وتَعالى كانَ ولا شَيءَ غَيرُهُ ، نوراً لا ظَلامَ فيهِ ، وصادِقاً لا كِذبَ فيهِ ، وعالِماً لا جَهلَ فيهِ، وحَيّاً لا مَوتَ فيهِ ، وكذلِكَ هُوَ اليَومُ ، وكذلِكَ لا يَزالُ أبَداً.
_source.english: Imam al-Baqir (AS) said, ‘Verily Allah, Blessed and most High, existed when nothing else did, He is light not darkness, truthful with no falsehood about Him, all-knowing with no ignorance about Him, ever-living with no death about Him, and He is such today, and thus will He remain forever.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): إنَّ اللّهَ عِلمٌ لا جَهلَ فيهِ ، حَياةٌ لا مَوتَ فيهِ ، نورٌ لا ظُلمَةَ فيهِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, ‘Verily Allah is all knowledge with no ignorance about Him, He is all Life without any death around Him, and all Light with no darkness about Him.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الكاظمُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): كانَ اللّهُ حَيّاً بِلا حَياةٍ حادِثَةٍ ... بَل حَيٌّ لِنَفسِهِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Kazim (AS) said, ‘Allah is Omnipresent without any external source of life … rather He lives through Himself.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): ولا يَعزُبُ عَنهُ عَدَدُ قَطرِ الماءِ، ولا نُجومُ السَّماءِ ، ولا سَوافِي الرِّيحِ في الهَواءِ ، ولا دَبيبُ النَّملِ عَلَى الصَّفا ، ولا مَقيلُ الذَّرِّ في اللّيلَةِ الظَّلماءِ ، يَعلَمُ مَساقِطَ الأوراقِ ، وخَفِيَّ طَرْفِ الأحداقِ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘The number of droplets of water, or of stars in the sky, or of gusts of wind in the air are not unknown to Him, and neither is the crawling of ants on rocks, nor the settling place of tiny particles in the darkness of the night. He knows the spots where leaves fall and the subtle movement of the pupils of the eyes.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): يَعلَمُ عَجيجَ الوُحوشِ في الفَلَواتِ، ومَعاصِيَ العِبادِ في الخَلَواتِ ، واختِلافَ النِّينانِ في بحار الأنوار الغامِراتِ ، وتَلاطُمَ الماءِ بِالرِّياحِ العاصِفاتِ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘He knows the howls of beasts in the forests, the sins of the people committed in secret, the fishs frequenting the deep seas and the rising of the waters by tempestuous winds.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): خَرَقَ عِلمُهُ باطِنَ غَيبِ السُّتُراتِ ، وأحاطَ بِغُموضِ عَقائدِ السَّريراتِ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘His knowledge pierces through the inside of unknown secrets and encompasses the innermost beliefs of the hearts.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الباقرُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): لَم يَزَلْ عالِماً بِما يَكونُ، فعِلمُهُ بِهِ قَبلَ كَونِهِ كعِلمِهِ بِهِ بَعدَ كَونِهِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Baqir (AS) said, ‘He always knows what is to be, such that His knowledge of it before its coming into being is the same as His knowledge after its coming into being.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ لَمّا سُئلَ عَن عِلمِهِ بِالمَكانِ: أكانَ قَبلَ تَكوينِهِ أم حِينَهُ وبَعدَهُ ؟ ـ: تَعالَى اللّهُ ! بَل لَم يَزَلْ عالِماً بِالمَكانِ قَبلَ تَكوينِهِ كَعِلمِهِ بِهِ بَعدَ ما كَوَّنَهُ، وكَذلِكَ عِلمُهُ بِجَميعِ الأشياءِ كعِلمِهِ بِالمَكانِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) was once asked about Allahs knowledge of space [i.e. the concept] and whether He knows it before its coming into existence or during it or after it, to which he replied, ‘Most High is Allah! He always knows space before its conception just as He knows it after He has created it, and such is His knowledge of all things like His knowledge of space.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): والعِلمُ ذاتُه ولا مَعلومَ ... فلَمَّا أحدَثَ الأشياءَ وكانَ المَعلومُ وَقَعَ العِلمُ مِنهُ عَلَى المَعلومِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said, ‘Knowledge is His very essence and not the object of knowing [or a known], such that when He created things, knowledge projected from Him onto the known things.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الكاظمُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): عِلمُ اللّهِ لا يُوصَفُ مِنهُ بِأينَ ، ولا يُوصَفُ العِلمُ مِنَ اللّهِ بِكَيفَ، ولا يُفرَدُ العِلمُ مِنَ اللّهِ، ولا يُبانُ اللّهُ مِنهُ ، ولَيسَ بَينَ اللّهِ وبَينَ عِلمِهِ حَدٌّ .
_source.english: Imam al-Kazim (AS) said, ‘The knowledge of Allah cannot be defined by where, nor can Allahs knowledge be described by how. Allahs knowledge cannot be separated from Him, nor can Allah be distinguished from it, and there is no barrier between Allah and His knowledge.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): وأشهَدُ أنَّهُ عَدلٌ عَدَلَ، وحَكَمٌ فَصَلَ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘And I bear witness that He is just and acts justly, and is an arbitrator who decides fairly.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ لَمّا سُئلَ عنِ العَدلِ ـ: العَدلُ إلّا تَتَّهِمَهُ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) when asked about faith in Allahs divine justice, replied, ‘[Faith in] divine justice is that you do not accuse Him of anything.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ زينَ العابدينُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ في دُعائهِ يَومَ الأضحى والجُمعَةِ ـ: وقَد عَلِمتُ أنَّهُ لَيسَ في حُكمِكَ ظُلمٌ ، ولا في نَقمَتِكَ عَجَلَةٌ ، وإنّما يَعجَلُ مَن يَخافُ الفَوتَ، وإنَّما يَحتاجُ إلَى الظُّلمِ الضَّعيفُ ، وقَد تَعالَيتَ يا إلهي عَن ذلكَ عُلُوّاً كَبيراً.
_source.english: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) said in his supplication for Friday and for the Aayd al-Azha, ‘But I know that there is no wrong in Your decree and no hurry in Your vengeance. He alone hurries who fears to miss, and only the weak needs to wrong. But You are exalted, my God, high indeed above all that!

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ وقد سُئلَ عَن أساسِ الدِّينِ ـ: التَّوحيدُ والعَدلُ . . . أمّا التَّوحيدُ فأن لا تُجَوِّزَ عَلى رَبِّكَ ما جازَ عَلَيكَ ، وأمّا العَدلُ فأن لا تَنسِبَ إلى خالِقِكَ ما لامَكَ عَلَيهِ.
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) was asked about the foundation of religion, to which he replied, ‘[It is faith in] Allahs divine Unity and divine Justice … [Faith in] Allahs divine Unity is that you do not deem applicable to your Lord that which applies to you, and [faith in] His divine Justice is that you do not attribute to Him that of which you are blameworthy.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الرِّضا (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): الحَمدُ للّهِ فاطِرِ الأشياءِ إنشاءً ، ومُبتَدِعِها ابتِداءً بِقُدرَتِهِ وحِكمَتِهِ ، لا مِن شَيءٍ فَيَبطُلَ الاختِراعُ ، ولا لِعِلَّةٍ فلا يَصِحَّ الابتِداعُ ، خَلَقَ ما شاءَ كَيفَ شاءَ .
_source.english: Imam al-Rida (AS) said, ‘The Originator of all things from their conception, and their Inventor from the very beginning with His Power and Wisdom, [He creates] not from anything otherwise the very concept of invention would be nullified, nor for any cause otherwise the very concept of origination would be inapplicable. He creates whatever He pleases however He pleases.

_source.arabic: المَسيحُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ لمّا قيل لَهُ: هل يقدرُ ربُّك على أن يدخل الدنيا في بيضةٍ ـ: إنَّ اللّهَ تَبارَكَ وتَعالى لا يُنسَبُ إلَى العَجزِ ، والّذي سَألتَني لا يَكونُ.
_source.english: Prophet Jesus (AS) was once asked, ‘Can your Lord fit the world into an egg? to which he replied, ‘Verily Allah, Mighty and Exalted, cannot be attributed with incapacity, but that which you are asking cannot ever be.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الصّادقُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): إنَّ إبليسَ قالَ لِعيسَى ابنِ مَريَمَ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): أيَقدِرُ رَبُّكَ عَلى أن يُدخِلَ الأرضَ بَيضَةً؛ لا يُصغِّرُ الأرضَ ولا يُكَبِّرُ البَيضَةَ ؟ فقالَ عيسى (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): وَيلَكَ ! إنَّ اللّهَ لا يُوصَفُ بِعَجزٍ ، ومَن أقدَرُ مِمَّن يُلَطِّفُ الأرضَ ويُعَظِّمُ البَيضَةَ؟!
_source.english: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrated, ‘Iblis [Satan] asked Jesus son of Mary (AS), ‘Is your Lord capable of fitting the earth inside an egg, without shrinking the earth or enlarging the egg? So Jesus (AS) replied, ‘Woe betide you! Verily Allah can never be ascribed with incapacity, and who is there more powerful than the One who can shrink the earth and enlarge the egg [if He so wills]?!

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): يُخبِرُ لا بِلِسانٍ ولَهَواتٍ، ويَسمَعُ لا بِخُروقٍ وأدَواتٍ ، يَقولُ ولا يَلفِظُ ، ويَحفَظُ ولا يَتَحَفَّظُ ... يَقولُ لِمَن أرادَ كَونَهُ: «كُنْ» فيَكونُ ، لا بِصَوتٍ يُقرَعُ ، ولا بِنِداءٍ يُسمَعُ ، وإنَّما كَلامُه سُبحانَهُ فِعلٌ مِنهُ ، أنشَأهُ ومَثَّلَهُ ، لَم يَكُنْ مِن قَبلِ ذلكَ كائناً، ولَو كانَ قَديماً لَكانَ إلهاً ثانِياً .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘He expresses information but not through a tongue or voice. He listens but not with the holes and organs of hearing. He speaks but does not utter words; He remembers but does not learn… When He wishes to create something, He says to it ‘Be and it is, but not through a voice that can strike the ears, nor a calling that can be heard. Rather, His speech, Glory be to Him, is an act of His that He creates and incorporates, which did not exist before, for were it an ever-existing thing it would be a second god.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الكاظمُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): إنَّما تَكونُ الأشياءُ بإرادَتِهِ ومَشيئَتِهِ ؛ مِن غَيرِ كلامٍ، ولا تَرَدُّدٍ في نَفَسٍ، ولا نُطقٍ بِلِسانٍ.
_source.english: Imam al-Kazim (AS) said, ‘Verily things come into being solely by His will and His wish; without the need for speech, alternation of breath or utterance with the tongue.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): الظّاهِرُ بِعَجائبِ تَدبيرِهِ لِلنّاظِرينَ ، والباطِنُ بِجَلالِ عِزَّتِهِ عَن فِكْرِ المُتَوَهِّمِينَ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘He manifests the wonders of His management for the onlookers, but by virtue of the exaltedness of His Might He is Hidden from the imagination of the thinkers.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الرِّضا (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): ظاهِرٌ لا بِتأويلِ المُباشَرَةِ ، مُتَجَلٍّ لا بِاستِهلالِ رُؤيَةٍ ، باطِنٌ لا بِمُزايَلَةٍ .
_source.english: Imam al-Rida (AS) said, ‘He is manifest though indiscernible through direct contact; He is evident though unapprehended by vision; He is hidden though not through withdrawal.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): كُلُّ مالِكٍ غَيرُهُ مَملوكٌ .
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘Every master other than Him is a slave.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌّ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ) ـ في تَفسيرِ لا حَولَ ولا قُوَّةَ إلّا بِاللّهِ ـ: إنّا لا نَملِكُ مَعَ اللّهِ شَيئاً ، ولا نَملِكُ إلّا ما مَلَّكَنا ، فمَتى مَلَّكَنا ما هُوَ أملَكُ بِهِ مِنّا كَلَّفَنا ، ومَتى أخَذَهُ مِنّا وَضَعَ تَكليفَهُ عَنّا.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS), in his explanation of the phrase ‘There is no power or strength save in Allah, said, ‘Verily we are not masters over anything with Allah, nor are we masters over anything except what He has given us mastery over. So by making us masters over that which He is a superior Master, He has given us responsibility, and by taking away mastership from us He absolves us of our responsibilities.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ عليٌ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): والسَّميعُ لا بِأداةٍ.
_source.english: Imam Ali (AS) said, ‘He is the All-hearing but not by means of any organ.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الباقرُ (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): إنَّهُ سَميعٌ بَصيرٌ ، يَسمَعُ بِما يُبصِرُ ، ويُبصِرُ بِما يَسمَعُ.
_source.english: Imam al-Baqir (AS) said, ‘Verily He is all-hearing and all-seeing, such that He hears with that by means of which He sees and He sees with that by means of which He hears.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الرّضا (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): لَمّا لَم يَخفَ عَلَيهِ خافِيَةٌ مِن أثَرِ الذَّرَّةِ السَّوداءِ ، عَلَى الصَّخرَةِ الصَّمّاءِ ، في اللَّيلَةِ الظَّلماءِ ، تَحتَ الثَّرى وبحار الأنوار ، قُلنا: بَصيرٌ .
_source.english: Imam al-Rida (AS) said, ‘Because of the fact that the secret trace of a black mustard seed on a massive rock in the darkness of the night, be it in the ground or in the seas, cannot remain hidden from Him, is what compels us to say that He is all-seeing.

_source.arabic: الإمامُ الرِّضا (عَلَيهِ الّسَلامُ): أمّا اللَّطيفُ فلَيسَ عَلى قِلَّةٍ وقَضافَةٍ وصِغَرٍ ، ولكِنَّ ذلِكَ عَلَى النَّفاذِ في الأشياءِ، والامتِناعِ مِن أن يُدرَكَ ، أمّا الخَبيرُ فالّذي لا يَعزُبُ عَنهُ شَيءٌ ولا يَفوتُهُ ، لَيسَ لِلتَّجرِبَةِ ولا لِلاعتِبارِ بِالأشياءِ ، فعِندَ التَّجرِبَةِ والاعتِبارِ عِلمانِ، ولَولاهُما ما عَلِمَ ؛ لأنَّ مَن كانَ كذلِكَ كانَ جاهِلاً.
_source.english: Imam al-Rida (AS) said, ‘He is subtle not in terms of lack or delicateness or smallness, rather [He is subtle] in His penetration into everything without being perceived. He is all-aware through the fact that nothing escapes His attention or evades Him, independent of experience or consideration of things, for experience and consideration in turn result in two types of knowledge, without which He would not know [if he were to be dependent on them], and would therefore be ignorant.
